reference.title: Low daily 10-mg and 20-mg doses of fluvoxamine inhibit the metabolism of both caffeine (cytochrome P4501A2) and omeprazole (cytochrome P4502C19).
reference.abstract: No convincing evidence was found that CYP2D6 is an important enzyme for the disposition of fluvoxamine. Other factors seem to be more important. A nontherapeutic oral daily dose of fluvoxamine is sufficient to provide a marked inhibition of both caffeine (CYP1A2) and omeprazole (CYP2C19) metabolism. It was not possible to separate the inhibitory effects of fluvoxamine on these enzymes, even after such a low daily dose such as 10 mg x 1 or x 2 of fluvoxamine.
